title: 1921 Portuguese legislative election
summary: The election of 10 July 1921 returned the Republican Liberal Party, formed months earlier by the merger of the Republican Union with the Evolutionists, as the largest in a parliament of 163 deputies with 79 of them, against a Democratic Party that had held the chamber for most of the Republic's life. The government it produced, under António Granjo, was three months old when a column of sailors and soldiers went through Lisbon on the night of 19 October and killed him and five others. It is in the atlas as the ballot behind the Noite Sangrenta: the last attempt of the First Republic to govern from a majority other than the Democrats', ended by murder rather than by a vote.
